title: Grandfather's Bicycle
text:
The bicycle had been standing in the corridor for as long as I could remember. Its paint had faded from blue to a dull grey, and the bell no longer rang properly.
My mother wanted to throw it away. My grandfather would not hear of it.
He had bought that bicycle more than fifty years ago, he told me, with three months of wages. He had ridden it to the factory every morning before the sun came up, and home again after dark. Once, he carried my mother on the back all the way to the hospital when she broke her arm.
Last month we cleaned it together. We oiled the chain, pumped the tyres, and polished the frame until it almost shone. My grandfather is too old to ride it now.
But he stood back, looked at it for a long moment, and said it was the best money he had ever spent.
